newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products strong, no weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products strong, no weakness seen.

text.p: Med oil products were uniformly strong on Monday.

Gasoline was firm with unleaded 98 octane material tight due to good prompt demand and a supply shortage caused by weak reforming margins. But the lower octane market was relaxed with plenty of cargo avails, traders said.

Naphtha remained strong, buoyed by firm crude and closure of Algeria's Skikda terminal due to high winds. The port has been closed since last week and is expected to reopen late Tuesday. "None of the lifters from Skikda have yet been forced into the market to buy spot, but it's still supportive," a trader said.
A Moroccan cargo was rumoured traded between a major refiner and a trading house into Portugal between cif quotes high +$4/$5 a tonne, cif Portugal.
Gas oil was firm, partly due to strong demand in northern Europe, and partly because most of the prompt Russian cargoes weighing on the market last week have been sold, traders said.
Trade was thin, but local markets were buoyed by another Turkish tender, this time to buy 75,000 tonnes 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil for delivery by Oct 25.
A trader offered an Italian heating oil cargo at Nov IPE +$6 cif Med, but traders said this was at the lower end of values.
Although supplies of fuel oil were seen a touch better the situation remains essentially tight and prices were stronger.

ISAB cargoes were heard offered around high cif Med +$2 cif Med. Buyers were looking for fixed price quotes of around $116 fob Med. Potenial demand of up to 500,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel this winter was seen to be bullish, although the perennial question of funding was uppermost in most traders' minds.
Low sulphur fuel was firm with dealers expectant of fresh interest from the main Med buyer.
